evidence.claim: CNAS reported that the defense industrial base remains shallow and fragile, with subtier suppliers still reliant on uneven demand signals and appropriations; it also stated that the average DoD supply chain spans five to six tiers while visibility is lost beyond tier two.

A media report alleged that GE Aerospace has been reviewing suppliers on quality, delivery, OSHA compliance, and percentage of domestically sourced raw materials. This is a useful lead but should not be treated as confirmed without GE, prime-contractor, or filing-level corroboration.
evidence.source_title: GE Aerospace’s Secret Supplier Shakeout Is Rattling Ohio’s Factory Belt – USA Business Times

evidence.claim: Howmet’s 2025 Form 10-K describes jet-engine components, aerospace fastening systems, airframe structural components, nickel/titanium/aluminum/cobalt products, and vertically integrated titanium-related engineered structures for aerospace and defense applications.

ATI’s 2025 Form 10-K says its HPMC segment produces high-performance specialty materials, including titanium and titanium-based alloys, nickel/cobalt superalloys, advanced powder alloys, seamless tubes, precision forgings, components, and machined parts, with about 92% of HPMC 2025 revenue from aerospace and defense markets.

Aluminum Market Update reported that Kaiser Aluminum had aerospace and high-strength shipments in 2025, including full-year shipments of 204.8 million pounds and fourth-quarter deliveries of 46.8 million pounds.
evidence.source_title: Kaiser Aluminum 2025 mix shift sets up 2026 plate and coated sheet growth

Ducommun stated in April 2025 that 95% of its revenue was derived from U.S.-based operations and reaffirmed its commitment to its U.S. manufacturing footprint.

memory_update.text: HWM should be retained as a reference/control name for aerospace/defense material traceability because it discloses engine products, fasteners, castings, titanium/aluminum structures, and vertically integrated titanium-related engineered structures.
ATI is a high-priority underfollowed materials candidate for the node because its HPMC segment maps directly to titanium alloys, superalloys, forgings, machined parts, and aerospace/defense demand.

DCO is a small-cap subtier supplier worth tracking for domestic manufacturing footprint, aerostructure machining, and supplier-consolidation exposure; verify customer/program dependence and material traceability disclosures.
Need stronger primary evidence for KALU’s defense-specific aerospace aluminum exposure, prime approvals, and domestic-origin traceability before it can move beyond hypothesis.

The core chokepoint is not only raw material availability but auditable origin documentation, qualification history, quality compliance, delivery reliability, and prime-contractor visibility into subtier suppliers.

summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around domestic-source documentation, aerospace/defense material compliance, and supplier qualification chokepoints. The strongest mapping is not to primes themselves but to subtier materials, forgings, castings, machined structures, and certified aerostructure suppliers that can document U.S. manufacturing footprint, titanium/aluminum/superalloy inputs, quality systems, and delivery reliability. CNAS evidence supports the broad fragility thesis: DoD supply chains often run five to six tiers deep while visibility weakens beyond tier two. Company-level evidence is strongest for Howmet and ATI, moderate for Ducommun, and more hypothesis-driven for Kaiser Aluminum as an aluminum plate/high-strength material node.
